 Ivory Coast release defender Emmanuel Agbadou ahead of Gambia return clash
 Sylvester Ntim 
 November 16, 2026 
 Share This Article: 
 Ivory Coast defender Emmanuel Agbadou has been released from the national team squad after sustaining thigh and knee injuries during the ongoing international break. 
 The Besiktas centre-back will no longer be part of the Elephants’ preparations for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against The Gambia after being granted permission to return to his club in Turkey for further medical attention.
 The Ivorian Football Federation confirmed the development in a statement issued on Sunday, November 15, following an assessment by the national team’s medical staff.
 According to the federation, Agbadou has been experiencing discomfort in his thigh and knee, prompting the medical team to recommend his release as a precautionary measure.
 The decision was taken in the best interests of the defender, allowing him to return to Besiktas and receive the necessary treatment under the supervision of his club’s medical department.
 His absence represents a setback for head coach Emerse Faé as Ivory Coast prepare for the return fixture against The Gambia on Tuesday, November 17.
 The Elephants head into the encounter with a narrow advantage after securing a 2-1 victory over the Scorpions in the first leg played in Bouaké on November 12.
 Agbadou’s withdrawal means Ivory Coast will have to make adjustments to their defensive options as they seek another positive result to strengthen their position in the qualifying campaign.
 The Ivorian technical team will now have to navigate the crucial encounter without the 29-year-old defender, whose recovery will be the immediate priority following his return to club duty.
